title: The Pythagorean theorem
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.geo.pythag.hypotenuse: a² + b² = c²: square the two shorter sides, add, then take the square root.
hints.geo.pythag.leg: c² − a² = b²: square both, subtract, then take the square root.
hints.geo.pythag.converse: Square the two shorter sides and add. If that equals the longest side squared, it's a right triangle.
hints.geo.pythag: a² + b² = c², with c the longest side. Square, add or subtract, then square root.

misconceptionMessages.geo.pythag-added: Don't add the sides: square them first (a² + b² = c²), then take the square root.
misconceptionMessages.geo.pythag-no-root: That's c². Take the square root to get c.
misconceptionMessages.geo.pythag-subtract-sides: Subtract the squares, not the sides: b² = c² − a².
misconceptionMessages.geo.pythag-wrong-side: Use the longest side as c, wherever it's written in the list.

similarProblemIntro: Here's the worked solution. Now try one like it.

sections.title: Find the hypotenuse
sections.objective: Find the longest side of a right triangle.
explain: In any right triangle, the squares on the two legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse (the side across from the right angle).
sections.key: a² + b² = c². Square the legs, add them, then take the square root.

sections.title: Find a leg
sections.objective: Find a shorter side of a right triangle.
explain: When you know the hypotenuse, subtract instead of adding.
sections.key: b² = c² − a². Square both, subtract, then take the square root.

sections.title: Is it a right triangle?
sections.objective: Tell whether three sides make a right triangle.
explain: The theorem works backwards too: if a² + b² = c² with c the longest side, the triangle has a right angle.
sections.key: Square the two shorter sides and add. Equal to the longest side squared? Then it's a right triangle.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: a² + b² = c², with c the longest side.
